recipes.name: Bacon Wrapped Pineapple
ingredients_raw: 1 (20 ounce) can pineapple chunks in juice, drained
0.5 pound sliced bacon, cut into thirds

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Wrap each pineapple chunk with 1 piece bacon; secure with toothpicks. Place in a shallow baking dish.
Combine brown sugar, mayonnaise, and chili sauce in a small bowl; pour over bacon-wrapped pineapple.
Bake in the preheated oven, uncovered, until bacon is crispy on the edges and sauce is bubbly, 25 minutes; serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Bacon Wrapped Pineapple
raw_recipe.description: This bacon-wrapped pineapple recipe wraps pineapple pieces in bacon, then roasts them in a sweet sauce with brown sugar, mayonnaise, and chili sauce.

review.reviewBody: My whole family loved these. I especially loved the sauce. I did find that they took a bit longer to bake than the recomended time. And, because I loved the sauce so much, but hated all of the bacon grease, what I did was cook them with half of the sauce first. Then, a few minutes before they were done, I transfered them into another pan dabbing off any grease onto a paper towel. Then I poured the remaining sauce over them in the new pan. It got rid of them sitting in the grease and the sauce didn't just bake onto the pan, it stayed on the wraps.

I made this last week for a holiday lunch at work. I wrapped the pineapple chunks with bacon, secured them with a toothpick and put them on a broiler pan. I cooked them for 30 minutes at 375º. Then I made the sauce using another's comments of 3/4 cup chili sauce to 1/3 cup brown sugar, and skipped the mayo altogether. I also added some cinnamon to the mix. Pulled the pan out and brushed on the sauce. Then back in for about 20 minutes more. Then pulled out and let cool.

Took them to work - all 20 or so (I had to taste a couple!). I was worried that folks might pass them by. Ha! They lasted all of 10 minutes; gone in a flash. 

I would definitely make them again, but here's my lessons learned. Instead of cutting the bacon strips in thirds, I'd cut them in half. This would give more bacon to wrap around and overlap. With the thirds, sometimes the ends barely met. Also, I opted to go with the applewood smoked bacon and that made it even tastier. I saw another's comment about getting sliced pineapple in a can and then cutting it into quarters for larger chunks. I might try that. The chunks from the can worked fine, but sometimes they can be small. When I pulled them out to put the sauce on, there were some that were stuck to the pan, so I might try PAM or moving them to another pan or dish for the final cooking stage. And aluminum foil in the broiler pan made cleanup so easy. At the end, I used a spatula to get them off the pan after they cooled. Next time, I would do that while

Absolutely wonderful. Used fresh pineapple. Placed wraps on a broiler pan(as suggested), spooned some sauce on each, baked for about 20-30 min at 375, transferred to another dish (stoneware) poured rest of sauce over and baked another 20 min or so until the sauce was carmelized. YUM, YUM, YUM. Never again will a pineapple go bad in my house!

These were awesome! Definitely a big hit at our small group get-together tonight - this platter was the first one emptied! I would suggest halving the sauce - it made way more than I needed. And definitely use a broiler pan (lined with foil) to bake - I actually broiled mine for 2 minutes after the timer went off to make sure the bacon got a little crispy. Perfect!!

The flavor is excellent, but I did make some modifications. First, I cooked the pinapple wrapped with bacon in the oven without the sauce for 30 minutes. I used 3/4 cup chili sauce to 1/3 cup brown sugar, and left out the mayo. The bacon made the dish greasy enough. After thirty minutes cook time, I drained the pineapple wraps on a paper towel. Because of the grease, I refreshed the foil liner in the baking pan, then returned the pinapple wraps and brushed them with the sauce. I then broiled them for about 5 minutes to get a little more "crisp" going on. Hubby was my guinia pig. He LOVED them. I also experimented by wrapping whole water chestnuts, and also wrapping shrimp. Nice contrast to the pinapple, and also adored by my guinia pig. I do have to say that these are a little time consuming to make, but can be made ahead, then reheated before serving. I plan to serve all three at my daughter's engagment party. Great base of a recipe. Thanks for posting it!

I wrapped these the night before and the bacon seemed to disappear. I don’t know if the acid in the pineapple disintegrated the bacon fat or what, but a word to the wise - don’t wrap a day ahead!! I’m sure with the bacon intact these would taste totally different but with only a little bacon left on these the pineapple with the sauce was not a tasty treat.

Excellent! They went fast at my party and everyone loved them. I did use the suggestion of baking them on a broiler pan or on a wire grate with a baking pan under. After 25 min. I transfered them to a corningware dish, poured 1/2 the sauce and cooked another 5 min. I used the other 1/2 of the sauce as a dip. I highly recommend this dish!
Good dish for a beach theme party. Next time, I would not use the mayo, but add a hoisin and honey sauce. Dont forget to use a broiler pan to drain off the grease.

I was skeptical of how many super-positive reviews there were - the ingredients seemed a bit too simple to yield such impressive results. I was wrong! People raved about how juicy, flavorful, and "addictive" these were. We even had a dedicated vegetarian guest try them (and then eat 7 more afterwards!!!). 
They're not overly pretty, but they taste fancy. The only thing I did differently was that I made the sauce and marinated the pineapple and bacon in it for a couple hours, then pulled them out, skewered them, and cooked them on a baking sheet. I didn't like the idea of them simmering in the greasy sauce - and they still turned out juicy and delicious!

This was good, but maybe not my personal preference. I prefer bacon wrapped water chestnuts. But those at the BBQ raved about them and said they were their favorite thing wrapped in bacon! I marinated the pineapple in the sauce and then wrapped the chunks in bacon that had been partially cooked in the microwave. Then I served the remaining sauce for dipping. The dipping sauce really made it good.

Baked bacon and pineapple w/o sauce just because I need to serve later. I put the sauce on the bottom of crock pot then put the bacon/pineapple on top---worked great(the sauce is awesome!!!!) thanks for a fun recipe--you can never have too much bacon!
I didn’t use Mayo. The pineapple and bacon didn’t taste great together like I hoped. If I were to do it again I would season the pineapple rather than the bacon.
Everyone raved about these when I brought them to a cookout, no leftovers. You do have to cook them longer to get the bacon crispy though.
They were ok
Excellent as is. Great appetizer!

This did not work for me. I tried to use fresh pineapple, maybe that was a mistake. The bacon fell off the pineapple during cooking and there was a ton of juice in the bottom of the pan making everything soft and mushy. The bacon just broke apart and slid off the fruit.
Very good and easy !
Mmmm didn't have chili sauce, found a recipe online for it... put over rice, we only had bacon in the house lol
These were AMAZING!! Make extra sauce for dipping! Will be making these again for sure!
so much flavor with or without sauce
